CUDA's default device heap is 8 MB, which overflows # above ~30k particles (illegal memory access). Must be set before the first kernel. CUDA.limit!(CUDA.LIMIT_MALLOC_HEAP_SIZE, 2^31) x0 = ensure_inputs()["x"] # shared Float64 correctness input, 2×1000 p0 = Params(size(x0, 2)) ``` ::: {#setup .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` Params{Float64}(10.0, 0.5, 1.0, 10.0, 10) ``` ::: ::: ::: {#cell-loss-cpu .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} # The whole pipeline is differentiated: cell ids, counting sort, gather into sorted # order, and neighbour loops whose ranges depend on the data. function sph_loss(x::AbstractMatrix{T}, p::Params{T}) where {T} N, nc = size(x, 2), p.nc s, rc = p.L / nc, 2 * p.h # 1. cell id of every particle, and particles per cell cell = Vector{Int}(undef, N) start = zeros(Int, nc * nc + 1) @inbounds for i in 1:N cx = mod(floor(Int, x[1, i] / s), nc) cy = mod(floor(Int, x[2, i] / s), nc) cell[i] = 1 + cx + nc * cy start[cell[i] + 1] += 1 end # 2. counting sort by cell: start[c] is the first sorted index of cell c start[1] = 1 for c in 1:nc * nc start[c + 1] += start[c] end cursor = start[1:end-1] perm = Vector{Int}(undef, N) @inbounds for i in 1:N perm[cursor[cell[i]]] = i cursor[cell[i]] += 1 end # 3. gather positions into sorted order: each cell is contiguous in memory xs = similar(x) @inbounds for k in 1:N xs[1, k] = x[1, perm[k]] xs[2, k] = x[2, perm[k]] end # 4. density and loss over the 3×3 neighbouring cells; each cell is the range # start[c]:start[c+1]-1, whose length depends on the data loss = zero(T) @inbounds for k in 1:N c = cell[perm[k]] - 1 cx, cy = c % nc, c ÷ nc ρ = zero(T) for dy in -1:1, dx in -1:1 cn = 1 + mod(cx + dx, nc) + nc * mod(cy + dy, nc) for l in start[cn]:start[cn + 1] - 1 rx = minimg(xs[1, k] - xs[1, l], p.L) ry = minimg(xs[2, k] - xs[2, l], p.L) r2 = rx * rx + ry * ry if r2 < rc * rc ρ += p.m * W(sqrt(r2), p.h) end end end loss += (ρ - p.ρ0)^2 end return loss end ``` ::: {#loss-cpu .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` sph_loss (generic function with 1 method) ``` ::: ::: ::: {#grad-cpu .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} function sph_gradient(x::Matrix{T}, p::Params{T}) where {T} dx = zero(x) Enzyme.autodiff(Reverse, sph_loss, Active, Duplicated(x, dx), Const(p)) return dx end g_cpu = sph_gradient(x0, p0) @printf "loss = %.10f ‖∇loss‖ = %.6f\n" sph_loss(x0, p0) sqrt(sum(abs2, g_cpu)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` loss = 12476.3617428793 ‖∇loss‖ = 7526.066606 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#cell-loss-gpu .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} # Same algorithm as KernelAbstractions kernels. The cell list is integer-valued (zero # derivative), so it is built outside the differentiated function with CUDA.jl's sort. # The gather and the neighbour loops are differentiated. # Box size, smoothing length etc. are not differentiated; declaring that lets Params be # passed to GPU kernels, which reject active (differentiable) scalar arguments. Enzyme.EnzymeRules.inactive_type(::Type{<:Params}) = true @kernel function cell_ids!(cell, counts, @Const(x), s, nc) i = @index(Global) @inbounds begin cx = mod(unsafe_trunc(Int32, floor(x[1, i] / s)), Int32(nc)) cy = mod(unsafe_trunc(Int32, floor(x[2, i] / s)), Int32(nc)) cell[i] = Int32(1) + cx + Int32(nc) * cy KernelAbstractions.@atomic counts[cell[i] + 1] += Int32(1) end end function build_cells(x::CuMatrix{T}, p::Params{T}) where {T} N, nc = size(x, 2), p.nc cell = CuVector{Int32}(undef, N) counts = CUDA.zeros(Int32, nc * nc + 1) cell_ids!(get_backend(x))(cell, counts, x, p.L / nc, nc; ndrange=N) counts[1:1] .= 1 perm = sortperm(cell) return (; perm=Int32.(perm), cell=cell[perm], start=cumsum(counts)) end @kernel function gather!(xs, @Const(x), @Const(perm)) k = @index(Global) @inbounds xs[1, k] = x[1, perm[k]] @inbounds xs[2, k] = x[2, perm[k]] end @kernel function density_loss!(e, @Const(xs), @Const(cellk), @Const(start), p) k = @index(Global) T, nc = eltype(xs), Int32(p.nc) @inbounds begin c = cellk[k] - Int32(1) cx, cy = c % nc, c ÷ nc ρ = zero(T) for dy in Int32(-1):Int32(1), dx in Int32(-1):Int32(1) cn = Int32(1) + mod(cx + dx, nc) + nc * mod(cy + dy, nc) for l in start[cn]:start[cn + 1] - Int32(1) # data-dependent range rx = minimg(xs[1, k] - xs[1, l], p.L) ry = minimg(xs[2, k] - xs[2, l], p.L) r2 = rx * rx + ry * ry if r2 < 4 * p.h * p.h ρ += p.m * W(sqrt(r2), p.h) end end end e[k] = (ρ - p.ρ0)^2 end end "Per-particle loss terms e (in sorted order); the loss is sum(e)." function sph_terms!(e, xs, x, cells, p) backend, N = get_backend(x), size(x, 2) gather!(backend)(xs, x, cells.perm; ndrange=N) density_loss!(backend)(e, xs, cells.cell, cells.start, p; ndrange=N) return nothing end function sph_loss(x::CuMatrix{T}, p::Params{T}) where {T} e, xs = similar(x, size(x, 2)), similar(x) sph_terms!(e, xs, x, build_cells(x, p), p) return sum(e) end ``` ::: {#loss-gpu .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` sph_loss (generic function with 2 methods) ``` ::: ::: ::: {#grad-gpu .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} "Gradient of sum(e): reverse mode seeded with de = 1." function sph_gradient(x::CuMatrix{T}, p::Params{T}) where {T} N = size(x, 2) e, de = similar(x, N), CUDA.ones(T, N) xs, dxs = similar(x), CUDA.zeros(T, size(x)) dx = CUDA.zeros(T, size(x)) Enzyme.autodiff(Reverse, sph_terms!, Const, Duplicated(e, de), Duplicated(xs, dxs), Duplicated(x, dx), Const(build_cells(x, p)), Const(p)) return dx end g_gpu = Array(sph_gradient(CuArray(x0), p0)) @printf "max |∇_gpu − ∇_cpu| / max |∇_cpu| = %.1e\n" maximum(abs, g_gpu - g_cpu) / maximum(abs, g_cpu) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ::: {.ansi-escaped-output} ```{=html}
